root_cause.text: In `btrfs_map_block()` in the Btrfs volume-mapping path, an error check added after `btrfs_chunk_map_num_copies()` returned `-EINVAL` without releasing the newly looked-up `chunk_map`, causing a reference leak on that early-exit path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (io_geom.mirror_num > num_copies) return -EINVAL;` to `ret = -EINVAL; goto out;`, and the commit message explicitly says “if we return early with -EINVAL, we're not freeing the chunk map that we've just looked up.”

commit 0ae653fbec2b9fbc72c65a0c99528990bfb2136d
Author: Johannes Thumshirn <johannes.thumshirn@wdc.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 13 13:36:40 2024 +0200

    btrfs: reduce chunk_map lookups in btrfs_map_block()
    
    Currently we're calling btrfs_num_copies() before btrfs_get_chunk_map() in
    btrfs_map_block(). But btrfs_num_copies() itself does a chunk map lookup
    to be able to calculate the number of copies.
    
    So split out the code getting the number of copies from btrfs_num_copies()
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is an early return after a mirror/count check on a newly acquired chunk map without freeing that map. In this snippet, the relevant check is present as `num_copies = btrfs_chunk_map_num_copies(map); if (io_geom.mirror_num > num_copies) return -EINVAL;`, but it occurs immediately after `map = btrfs_get_chunk_map(...)` and there is still no `btrfs_free_chunk_map(map)` on the `-EINVAL` path. However, the specific bug in the root cause is about the old `btrfs_num_copies()` call and whether this commit already fixes that leak by moving the count computation to use the same `map`. Since the code shown still has the early-return-without-free pattern, the vulnerable construct is present. But this commit does not yet include any cleanup on that error path, so the fix is not present in this function body.
